behavioral_evidence.value: Directed item transitions in the training split: for each item i, the multiset of items s that occur immediately after i in a training user sequence, with their counts w_is (sequential co-consumption of a directed, successor form). Nothing else; no user ids, no timestamps, no popularity signal.

One pass over the training split sequences only (the same split the encoder is trained on). For every adjacent pair (i, s) inside a training sequence increment w_is; store S_i as a sparse row of (s, w_is). W_i = sum_s w_is. No pruning threshold and no top-K: all successors are kept with their counts, so no tuned constant enters. Successor ball points v_s are read from the per-epoch snapshot table indexed by item, so the field refreshes once per epoch and is detached.

S_i is built exclusively from adjacency pairs inside training-split sequences, computed once before training and frozen for the whole run; validation and test sequences are never read, never encoded into the snapshot, and never used to set q_l, m_i or the clip. The peer-c

lip uses min_k d_P(v_i, u_k) from the current training step only, so nothing about held-out interaction can influence the SID construction, the codebook, or the assigned identifiers. q_l is a percentile of training residuals at epoch 0, also training-only.

geometric_necessity.value: Fixed negative curvature c = 1.0 (K = -1), with the Poincare ball metric lambda(x) = 2/(1 - c||x||^2); operations: bounded exponential-style lift (1/sqrt(c)) tanh(sqrt(c)||r||/q_l) * r-hat, Mobius addition (+), geodesic distance d_P(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||), and tangent logarithm Log_x(y) used to build the behaviour direction. A trainable log-curvature per level (eta_l initialised at 0, c_l = exp(eta_l)) is available in code but left at its documented default, not swept.

In the quantisation step of the RQ-VAE, inside the Sinkhorn cost matrix of levels 2 and 3, before the balanced plan is solved; it changes both which code each fine level assigns (through the plan) and the gradient that reaches the residual encoder and the fine codebooks (through d_P and through the displacement).
C[i,k] = d_P^c( v_i , u_k (+) ( tanh(sqrt(c) m_i / 2)/sqrt(c) ) * n_i ), with m_i n_i = clip_{0.5 * min_j d_P(v_i,u_j)}( sum_s (w_is/W_i) Log_{v_i}(v_s) ).

implementation_cost.claim: declared cost of the frozen run
implementation_cost.value: Frozen scale 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch (about 1023 items per step), 3000 epochs. Per step: extra 2 levels * 1023 items * 256 codes = 524k Mobius-add + artanh + norm evaluations at d = 32, about 0.07 GFLOP, under 1% of the encoder forward+backward. Per epoch: one extra forward-only pass over all 24556 items (24 forward batches, no backward) to refresh the successor snapshot, about one third of an epoch's forward cost, so roughly +5% to +7% wall clock per epoch and about the same over the whole run. No extra epochs, no extra seeds, no extra arms.

prior_work.value: Not a cohesion bias on level 1, not a scalar behaviour offset added to a distance, not a second hyperbolic loss.
